title: paged KV cache: block allocator reuse, pinning, and TTL eviction optimizations
author: Diego Martinez
description: Motivation: reduce KV cache memory churn and tail latency under mixed workloads by reusing freed blocks, preventing hot-block eviction via pinning, and smoothing eviction with a lightweight TTL heuristic. This PR implements three coordinated changes: (1) allocator reuse across allocator pools to reduce fragmentation and allocation overhead when blocks are frequently freed/allocated; (2) an explicit pinning API and internal pin counters to keep hot blocks resident during concurrent reads and ongoing generation; (3) a lightweight TTL-based eviction modifier that prefers evicting cold blocks and delays eviction of recently accessed prefixes. The description below summarizes code changes, benchmarks, compatibility, and rollout plan. Key outcomes from internal benchmarks: +12% throughput on 8k token throughput synthetic workload, -18% p99 token latency in mixed read/write tail scenarios, and ~30% reduction in allocator-related churn in flame graphs. Backwards compatibility: behavior is guarded behind a runtime feature flag (kv.cache.new_allocator_reuse=true) and the pinning APIs are additive; default is enabled for this release after experimentation. Rollout: feature enabled on canary pool for 48h, then region rollouts with monitoring dashboards and automatic rollback conditions (memory spike > 15% or p99 regressions > 10%).

review_thread: Lina Chen: Nice consolidation — can you clarify how reuse interacts with different size classes? Potential ABA on freelist?
Diego Martinez: Reuse is partitioned per-size-class; we use a versioned freelist node and hazard-check on pop to avoid ABA, comment added with reference to hazard pointer design we discussed.
Ravi Patel: Pinning looks good but we need guardrails for memory blowup if many pins accumulate (eg streaming long conversations). Suggest TTL fallback to force-unpin after X minutes.

Diego Martinez: Added TTL heuristic that demotes long-pinned blocks after configurable duration and emits a caution metric. Default TTL is 10m for pinned blocks; operator can tune. See eviction_policy.rs change.
Samir Kapoor: Can we add unit tests for concurrent pin/unpin + eviction? Also add a perf benchmark against current master for p99.
Diego Martinez: Added stress test 'pinning_concurrency' and bench harness comparing this branch to main; attached perf results in PR description.

release_notes: Improve paged KV cache performance: reuse block allocator to reduce churn, add pinning to avoid hot-block eviction, and introduce a TTL-based eviction modifier. Results: ~12% throughput improvement and ~18% p99 latency reduction for mixed read/write workloads. Rollout controlled by kv.cache.new_allocator_reuse runtime flag.
notes: This PR touches low-level allocator paths; monitor allocator_free_rate, pinned_block_count, kv_cache_evictions, and p99_token_latency on canary after rollout.
